title: Naturality and connecting-square compatibility of projective-line duality maps
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $X=\mathbf P^1_k$, and $\omega=\Omega^1_{X/k}\cong\mathcal O_X(-2)$ as in [lem-sc-p1-monomial](iii). Fix a $k$-linear isomorphism $t:H^1(X,\omega)\to k$, which exists by [lem-sc-p1-monomial](ii),(iii). Write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, define $\alpha_{\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Hom}_X(\mathcal G,\omega)\to H^1(X,\mathcal G)^\vee$ by $\alpha_{\mathcal G}(\varphi)(c)=t(H^1(\varphi)(c))$. Define $\beta_{\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal G,\omega)\to H^0(X,\mathcal G)^\vee$ by $\beta_{\mathcal G}(e)(s)=t(e\circ s)$, where $s:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G$ represents a global section and $e\circ s\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal O_X,\omega)=H^1(X,\omega)$ via [lem-sc-ext-locally-free]; Ext is as in [def-sc-ext-sheaf]. Both families are contravariantly natural in $\mathcal G$. For every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, let $\partial_H:H^0(X,\mathcal C)\to H^1(X,\mathcal A)$ be the cohomology connecting map and $\partial_E:\operatorname{Hom}_X(\mathcal A,\omega)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal C,\omega)$ the Ext connecting map given by pushout of the extension. Then the square commutes with sign $+1$: $\beta_{\mathcal C}\circ\partial_E=(\partial_H)^\vee\circ\alpha_{\mathcal A}$. Equivalently, for $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\omega$ and $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal C)$, $t((\partial_E\varphi)\circ s)=t(H^1(\varphi)(\partial_Hs))$.

proof.text: The displayed formulas define the two pairings. The beta formula is well typed because [def-sc-ext-sheaf] supplies the Ext groups and [lem-sc-ext-locally-free] identifies $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal O_X,\omega)$ with $H^1(X,\omega)$.

proof.text: For $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\omega$, $\alpha_{\mathcal G'}(\varphi\circ u)(c)=t(H^1(\varphi\circ u)(c))=t(H^1(\varphi)(H^1(u)(c)))=\alpha_{\mathcal G}(\varphi)(H^1(u)(c))$ by functoriality of the derived cohomology functor and associativity of composition. This is contravariant naturality of $\alpha$.

source.place: proof, Step 2: naturality of the Cech pairing

proof.text: For $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$, $e\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal G,\omega)$ and $s:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G'$, the map $u^*=\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(u,\omega)$ sends $e$ to the Yoneda composite $e\circ u$ by [lem-sc-p1-ext-yoneda-functoriality], and $H^0(u)(s)=u\circ s$ as maps $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G$. Hence $\beta_{\mathcal G'}(u^*e)(s)=t((e\circ u)\circ s)=t(e\circ(u\circ s))=\beta_{\mathcal G}(e)(H^0(u)(s))$ by associativity of Yoneda composition [lem-sc-p1-ext-yoneda-associativity]. This is contravariant naturality of $\beta$.

source.place: proof, Step 2: naturality of the Yoneda pairing

proof.text: Given $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$, write $\delta\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal C,\mathcal A)$ for its extension class and identify $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal C)$ with $s:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal C$. [lem-sc-p1-boundary-extension-composition] gives $\partial_Hs=\delta\circ s$ in $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal A)=H^1(X,\mathcal A)$, and [lem-sc-p1-ext-yoneda-functoriality] gives $H^1(\varphi)(\delta\circ s)=\varphi[1]\circ(\delta\circ s)$ under the same identification, so $\alpha_{\mathcal A}(\varphi)(\partial_Hs)=t(\varphi[1]\circ(\delta\circ s))$. [lem-sc-p1-ext-yoneda-associativity] gives $\partial_E\varphi=\varphi[1]\circ\delta$ and $(\varphi[1]\circ\delta)\circ s=\varphi[1]\circ(\delta\circ s)$, so $\beta_{\mathcal C}(\partial_E\varphi)(s)=t((\varphi[1]\circ\delta)\circ s)$ is the same element. Hence $\beta_{\mathcal C}\circ\partial_E=(\partial_H)^\vee\circ\alpha_{\mathcal A}$ with sign $+1$ (with the conventions fixed in the cited statements: $\partial_E$ by pushout, $\partial_H$ the connecting map of cohomology).
